_meta.scale_note: Taste scores run from 0 to 1, so penalties are on the same scale: -0.1 to -0.15 is a small nudge that only reorders close calls, -0.2 to -0.3 moves a good match down the list, and -0.35 to -0.5 is strong enough that a perfect match drops below an ordinary one.

justification_types.inferred_from_source: Based on a real source, applied to films and hospital viewing.
justification_types.inferred: My own reasoning; no source says it in these words.

condition_vocabulary.content: flash_in | flash_conf | mpa_in | runtime_gt | runtime_lte | runtime_missing | pacing | intensity | theme_any | accessibility_unknown | accessibility_false

sources.ITC: ITC Guidance Note on Flashing Images and Regular Patterns in Television (hosted by Ofcom, rev. July 2001), paras 2, 3, 3.1.1 - https://www.ofcom.org.uk/__data/assets/pdf_file/0021/16248/gn_flash.pdf
sources.OFCOM212: Ofcom Broadcasting Code Rule 2.12, quoted in Ofcom Broadcast Bulletin 178 - https://www.ofcom.org.uk/siteassets/resources/documents/about-ofcom/bulletins/broadcast-bulletins/archive/obb178/obb178.pdf
sources.MPA: MPA Classification and Rating Rules, Section 3(C), pp. 7-8 - https://www.filmratings.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/rating_rules.pdf
sources.ACS: American Cancer Society, Getting Help for Fatigue - https://www.cancer.org/content/dam/cancer-org/cancer-control/en/what-to-do/getting-help-for-fatigue.pdf
sources.STAN: Stanford Children's Child Life Entertainment/Special Events Guidelines, items 5, 10, 12 - https://www.stanfordchildrens.org/content/dam/sch/content-public/pdf/Event_Guidelines.pdf
sources.CWI: Children's Wisconsin Entertainment and Visitor Guidelines (3/19/2021), 'The Day of your Visit' items 1 and 6 - https://childrenswi.org/-/media/chwlibrary/files/patient-family-experience/cl-entertainment-guidelines.pdf

rules.name: Light-sensitive patient, film has flashing
rules.notes: Flashing can set off seizures in people with photosensitive epilepsy, so these films are removed outright.

rules.name: Light-sensitive patient, flashing unknown
rules.source: OFCOM212 ('maintain a low level of risk'); ITC para 2
rules.notes: If we don't know whether a film has flashing, we don't risk it for this patient.

rules.name: Light-sensitive patient, minor flashing reported
rules.source: ITC para 2 (flashing over 5 seconds may be a risk even within limits); EF (triggers vary by person)
rules.notes: Even minor reported flashing is removed for this patient; the risk isn't worth one extra film.

rules.name: Light-sensitive patient, no flashing known but not confirmed
rules.notes: Films with stronger evidence of no flashing rank slightly above ones without it.

rules.name: Under 17, R-rated film
rules.source: MPA rules p.8: 'Restricted. Children Under 17 Require Accompanying Parent or Adult Guardian'
rules.notes: R-rated films are kept away from under-17s in a hospital setting, where no parent may be present to decide.

rules.name: Under 18, NC-17 film
rules.source: MPA rules p.8: 'No One 17 and Under Admitted'
rules.notes: Follows the rating board's own rule: nobody 17 or under.

rules.name: Under 13, PG-13 film
rules.source: MPA rules p.7: 'Parents Strongly Cautioned. Some Material May Be Inappropriate For Children Under 13'
rules.notes: PG-13 films can still be shown to under-13s, but rank lower.

rules.name: Seriously ill child, film about serious illness
rules.source: CWI item 6 (no themes such as violence, death, illness, medical care)
rules.notes: A child going through serious illness shouldn't be shown a film that is centred on serious illness.

rules.name: Adult with cancer, film about serious illness
rules.notes: Adults can choose for themselves, so this is a strong penalty rather than a removal.

rules.name: Child in hospital, hospital or medical scenes
rules.notes: Hospital and medical scenes rank lower for children who are already in hospital.

rules.name: Child in hospital, illness subplot
rules.notes: An illness subplot is lighter than a whole film about it, so the penalty is smaller.

rules.name: Child in hospital, death or loss
rules.source: STAN item 5 ('threatening themes such as death, violence or degradation'); CWI item 6
rules.notes: Death and loss rank lower for children, but these films aren't removed, since many classics include them.

rules.name: Child in hospital, violence
rules.notes: Violent themes rank lower for children in hospital.

rules.name: Child in hospital, very intense film
rules.notes: Very intense films rank lower for children in hospital.

rules.name: Young child, scary creatures
rules.source: Own reasoning, loosely following STAN item 10 (costumes and masks can frighten children).
rules.notes: Scary creatures rank lower for young children.

rules.name: Bereaved patient, death or loss
rules.notes: The patient has said this topic upsets them, so these films are removed.

rules.name: Anxious patient, scary or intense film
rules.content_attribute: scary_creatures OR visceral_gore theme OR thematic_intensity == 'high'
rules.notes: Scary, gory or very intense films rank well down for patients with anxiety.

rules.name: Very tired patient, film over 2.5 hours
rules.source: Own reasoning, based on the ACS description of cancer fatigue (exhausted, hard to focus, save your energy).
rules.notes: Very long films are hard to sit through when exhausted; they rank lower but can still be paused and finished.

rules.name: Very tired patient, film over 2 hours
rules.source: Own reasoning, based on ACS fatigue advice; the hospital guidelines suggest 20-40 minute events (STAN item 12, CWI item 1).
rules.notes: A smaller penalty for films that are long but not very long.

rules.name: Very tired patient, complicated plot
rules.source: Own reasoning, based on ACS ('can't focus').
rules.notes: Complicated plots are hard to follow when tired.

rules.name: Very tired patient, length not listed
rules.notes: A small penalty when a film's length isn't listed.

rules.name: Nauseous patient, gory scenes
rules.notes: Gory scenes rank well down for patients feeling sick from treatment.

rules.name: Nauseous patient, very intense film
rules.notes: Intense films rank lower for patients feeling sick from treatment.

rules.name: Needs subtitles, subtitles not listed
rules.notes: Films rank slightly lower when subtitle availability isn't listed.

rules.name: Needs subtitles, film has none
rules.notes: If a film definitely has no subtitles, it's removed for patients who need them.

rules.name: Needs audio description, not listed
rules.notes: Films rank slightly lower when audio description availability isn't listed.
